source.title: Geometry-aware similarity metrics for neural representations on Riemannian and statistical manifolds

record.file_problem: None noted; the complete 13-page paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares representation-similarity methods and reports that their conclusions differ, including high extrinsic similarity alongside low intrinsic similarity for rich and lazy networks. It refines the claim by showing that similarity assessments depend on the metric; it does not test convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports additional MSA comparisons for diffusion-model guidance and timepoints, but these compare changing dynamics within one diffusion model rather than convergence between independently trained models. Values visible only in the figures are not transcribed because the supplied text gives explicit qualitative descriptions for the relevant comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study introduces an intrinsic-geometry similarity measure, MSA, and compares it with Procrustes, RSA, CCA and DSA on the same network pairs. Extrinsic measures report high or intermediate similarity, even trained vs untrained, where MSA reports low or zero. This bears directly on V6, the dependence of measured similarity on the metric. Within-MSA comparisons across seeds also bear weakly on V3. There is no scale, cross-modal, mapping or feature-universality test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that extrinsic similarity measures can miss fundamental differences between network solutions, and that MSA, by comparing intrinsic geometry via pullback metrics, distinguishes them. They note MSA is correlational, needs a characterised input manifold, and ignores downstream use of the representation.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces MSA, based on pullback metrics and a spectral-ratio distance, rather than reproducing either original source's convergence method. It does not test convergence with scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported assessment of similarity changes with the chosen measure: MSA, Procrustes, RSA, CCA, and DSA give different comparisons in the reported experiments.
record.problems: The evidence concerns selected toy networks and task-trained RNN/SSM models, not models scaled by size or capability. Reported results are qualitative in the supplied text, with no uncertainty estimates. The authors state that MSA is correlational and does not establish causal mechanisms; its application also requires characterizing the input manifold.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results left out. Diffusion-model comparisons vary guidance or time within a model and do not test convergence between independently trained models.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; only toy networks and small task-trained RNN/SSMs.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability test.
No interpretable features or circuits compared.
No test of plateauing alignment or of shared data or objectives as its cause.
Neighbour count, input distribution and out-of-distribution inputs were not varied; only the choice of similarity measure was.
Shared features or subspaces versus individual units are not tested; only whole-representation intrinsic geometry is.

missing.what: Numeric similarity values for MSA, Procrustes, RSA, CCA and DSA (rich vs lazy, seeds, hierarchy, RNN/SSM) appear only in the figures, not in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The V7 label was removed: rich vs lazy dissimilarity concerns different learning regimes, not partial convergence or its causes. The study is not an original source. The diffusion-model results compare guidance levels and timepoints within a single model and are correctly excluded. All evidence is qualitative text, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no test of convergence across independently trained models as scale increases.
No paired image-caption comparison or vision-language model comparison.
The study compares geometric similarity across seeds in toy networks and RNNs, but does not test whether the networks learn shared features or subspaces.
No mapping between representations, stitching, or test of interchangeability.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The study compares MSA with Procrustes, RSA, CCA, and DSA in selected experiments. It does not systematically vary neighbour count, input distributions, or out-of-distribution inputs.

The study reports incomplete or differing similarity across learning regimes, tasks, and training stages. It does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared data/objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause alignment.
